answers.note: Деулинское перемирие 1618 года завершило войну России с Речью Посполитой.
Нерчинский договор 1689 года стал первым договором России с Китаем.

literal.prompt: Какой договор 1689 года стал первым соглашением России с Китаем?

finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: The retained official Presidential Library page identifies the Nerchinsk Treaty as the first Russia–China treaty and dates it 1689 (turn1view1 L40-L45). It also identifies the 1618 Deulino truce with Poland (turn1view0 L44-L47), while the retained official Crimea page says the Paris peace ended that war (turn3view3 L51), and the U.S. Department of State treaty text gives Brest Litovsk, 3 March 1918 and cessation of war between Russia and the Central Powers (turn3view0 L14-L18, L82). Thus only Nerchinsk matches both 1689 and Russia–China.
finalGroupBindings.locator: Nerchinsk turn1view1 L40-L45; Deulino turn1view0 L44-L47; Paris turn3view3 L51; Brest turn3view0 L14-L18,L82

finalGroupBindings.literal: Нерчинский договор 1689 года стал первым договором России с Китаем. Он определил условия отношений двух государств и наметил границу в Приамурье лишь в общих чертах.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: The official library page calls the 1689 Nerchinsk agreement the first Russia–China treaty (turn1view1 L40-L45), describes mutual trade and the border arrangements (L50), and explicitly qualifies the boundary as only sketched in general terms and unclear in places (L51-L52). The revised sentence preserves that qualification.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Деулинское перемирие 1618 года приостановило боевые действия России с Речью Посполитой на 14,5 года.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: The retained Deulino article says the Russian and Polish delegations concluded a truce for 14.5 years on 1 (11) December 1618 (turn1view0 L44-L47); it supports a truce that halted hostilities for that term, not an unconditional end to the Russo-Polish war.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Договором разрешалась взаимная торговля между подданными России и Цинской империи.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: The Nerchinsk page states that the treaty permitted mutual trade between subjects of Russia and the Qing Empire (turn1view1 L50). This is a concrete fact about the correct option beyond the prompt and key.

finalGroupBindings.literal: Парижский мирный договор 1856 года завершил Крымскую войну.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: The official Presidential Library page states that the Crimean War ended with the Paris peace treaty signed 18 (30) March 1856 (turn3view3 L51).

finalGroupBindings.literal: Статья 1 Брест-Литовского договора прекратила состояние войны между Россией и державами Центрального блока; договор подписали 3 марта 1918 года.
finalGroupBindings.primaryGround: Article 1 of the retained treaty says Russia and Germany, Austria-Hungary, Bulgaria, and Turkey declared the state of war between them ceased (turn3view0 L14-L18); the execution line dates the treaty 3 March 1918 (L80-L82).

authorAssessment.grammar: The prompt asks for a treaty; “Деулинское перемирие” is a standalone historical agreement name in nominative, matching the standalone-name form used by all four options. No case inflection is required after the completed question.
authorAssessment.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: A real interstate truce is a plausible same-category distractor. The source identifies it as a 1618 truce between Russia and Poland, not the 1689 Russia–China treaty. Its own note now accurately says it halted hostilities for 14.5 years; it cannot satisfy the prompt because its parties and date differ from the uniquely supported Nerchinsk event. The note teaches the Deulino truce’s actual duration and avoids the previous overstatement that it ended the war.

authorAssessment.grammar: “Нерчинский договор” is a natural nominative proper-name answer to “Какой договор”. All four options are names of historical interstate agreements.
authorAssessment.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: The answer is the only choice identified as the first Russia–China treaty of 1689. Deulino is 1618/Russia–Poland, Paris is 1856/Crimea, and Brest Litovsk is 1918/Russia–Central Powers; the distractors remain real agreements in the same broad category. The exact entity, relation, and value match only the Nerchinsk Treaty: first treaty between Russia and China, concluded in 1689. The note adds that the treaty allowed mutual trade between subjects of Russia and Qing China, a concrete fact not present in the prompt or answer label.
